docRequirement: network-config.md:30-33 documents TWO accepted spellings of the same variable, side by side: `# Bypass proxy for specific requests - space-separated format` / `export NO_PROXY="localhost 192.168.1.1 example.com .example.com"` and `# Bypass proxy for specific requests - comma-separated format` / `export NO_PROXY="localhost,192.168.1.1,example.com,.example.com"`. A `NO_PROXY` parser must therefore treat whitespace as an entry separator exactly as it treats a comma. The page's note `All environment variables shown on this page can also be configured in settings.json` extends the same contract to the settings-side field (our `NetworkProxySettings.noProxy`, packages/shared/src/config/types.ts:31).
current: Every NO_PROXY parser in the fork splits on commas only, on all three surfaces. (1) packages/shared/src/config/network-proxy-utils.ts:11-13 `splitCommaSeparated` is literally `str.split(',').map(s => s.trim()).filter(Boolean)`, and `parseNoProxyRules` calls it at :222 (its docblock at :210 says `Parse a comma-separated NO_PROXY string`); that feeds `currentTrust.noProxyRules` (network-runtime.ts:153) which `proxyForUrl` consults at :221 for every wrapped `fetch`, and the Electron `ProxyDispatcher` at apps/electron/src/main/network-proxy.ts:67. (2) packages/shared/src/unified-network-interceptor.ts:84-86 re-implements the parse as `NO_PROXY.split(',')` over the env value read at :69 (`process.env.NO_PROXY || process.env.no_proxy`); on a bypass miss `getProxyForUrl` (:106-109) returns PROXY_URL and the wrapper sets it as Bun's explicit `proxy:` fetch option (:2386, :2432-2434), so the request is ACTIVELY forced through the proxy rather than merely left to Bun's own env handling. (3) apps/electron/src/main/network-proxy.ts:216-218 builds Chromium's `proxyBypassRules` as `splitCommaSeparated(settings.noProxy).join(',')`, so every Electron session partition (browser pane, update feed, default) inherits the same single bogus rule. Nothing normalizes whitespace upstream: storage.ts:2556-2559 `normalizeProxyString` trims only the outer edges of the whole string (used for `noProxy` at :2571), and the Settings > Network > Bypass Rules field only `.trim()`s (AppSettingsPage.tsx:88, field at :394-400). Nothing warns: proxy logging is booleans only (network-proxy.ts:242-251 `hasNoProxy: true`) plus a debug-only line (interceptor :112). Measured on this rig just now against the page's own two example strings: the space form yields exactly one rule `{host:'localhost 192.168.1.1 example.com .example.com', wildcard:false}` and `shouldBypassProxy` returns false for http://localhost:3000/x, https://example.com, https://api.example.com/v1 and http://192.168.1.1/; the comma twin (positive control, same rig) yields four rules and returns true for all four.
divergence: Separator set only. The rule grammar itself is correct and complete — `*`, exact host, `.suffix`, `host:port`, IPv4, `[::1]`, `[::1]:port` all parse and match as documented (network-proxy-utils.ts:219-293, covered by network-proxy.test.ts:40-124). What is missing is that whitespace is not accepted as an entry delimiter, so one of the page's two documented spellings degrades to a single unmatchable rule instead of erroring. It is a silent narrowing, not a wrong value and not a wrong key name.

change.what: Add a NO_PROXY-specific splitter `function splitNoProxyEntries(str: string | undefined): string[] { if (!str) return []; return str.split(/[\s,]+/).map(s => s.trim()).filter(Boolean); }` and have `parseNoProxyRules` call it at :222 in place of `splitCommaSeparated`. Do NOT widen `splitCommaSeparated` itself (:11-13): it is shared with `parseCertStoreSources` (:37), whose documented separator on the same page is comma only — widening the shared helper would make `certStore` silently accept a spelling the doc does not define. Update the two docblocks that assert the separator: :10 stays comma-only, :210 must stop saying `Parse a comma-separated NO_PROXY string` and cite network-config.md:30-33 for both accepted spellings. One-line body plus two comment edits.

Change `NO_PROXY.split(',')` to `NO_PROXY.split(/[\s,]+/)`. One line. Keep the parser inline rather than importing the shared helper — this module is preloaded into the Pi subprocess and bundled standalone to apps/electron/dist/interceptor.cjs; add a comment naming network-proxy-utils.ts as the twin so the next separator change touches both.

Replace `splitCommaSeparated(settings.noProxy).join(',')` with the new `splitNoProxyEntries(settings.noProxy).join(',')` (import swap at :19). Keep the comma join — Chromium's bypass-rule parser is the consumer and comma is a separator it accepts; the defect is the pre-split, not the join.

Add one table-driven case running the page's OWN two example strings through `parseNoProxyRules` + `shouldBypassProxy`: `'localhost 192.168.1.1 example.com .example.com'` and its comma twin must produce identical rule arrays and both must bypass http://localhost:3000/x, https://example.com, https://api.example.com/v1, http://192.168.1.1/. Add one mixed/repeated-separator boundary case (`'localhost,  example.com\t.internal'`). Two tests, no more — the grammar itself is already covered at :40-124.

RECOMMENDED, not strictly required by the page: emit the CANONICAL comma-joined form (`splitNoProxyEntries(settings.noProxy).join(',')`) instead of the raw string. This env is spread into the Pi subprocess (agent/pi-agent.ts:1466), the Claude SDK options (agent/options.ts:241) and every MCP server subprocess (mcp/client.ts:398), whose own parsers are third-party and comma-only; without canonicalization a space-form setting keeps failing everywhere except our two patched parsers. Mirror it at network-runtime.ts:214 `assign(['NO_PROXY','no_proxy'], settings.noProxy)` if you take this. If skipped, say so in the plan — it is a knowingly partial fix.

`The **No proxy** field is a comma-separated list of bypass patterns` becomes comma- OR whitespace-separated. Same edit in the ru twin docs-site/content/ru/reference/config/network-proxy.md. The UI placeholder `settings.network.bypassPlaceholder` (en.json:1485, ru.json:1509) can stay as-is — the comma form remains valid and is the better prompt.

blastRadius: `parseNoProxyRules` has 3 callers in packages/shared/src/config/network-runtime.ts (the resolved `currentTrust.noProxyRules` at :153, read by `proxyForUrl` :218-223 inside the global `fetch` wrapper installed at :236-265) and one in apps/electron/src/main/network-proxy.ts:67 (`ProxyDispatcher`, the undici dispatcher for the Electron main process). `shouldBypassProxy` exists TWICE under that name — network-proxy-utils.ts:268 (shared, rule-object based) and unified-network-interceptor.ts:89 (Pi subprocess, string-pattern based); they are independent implementations and both must change. `splitCommaSeparated` is SHARED with `parseCertStoreSources` (network-proxy-utils.ts:37) — that is the trap: widening it changes certStore parsing, covered by __tests__/network-cert-store.test.ts. Tests that will see the change: packages/shared/src/config/__tests__/network-proxy.test.ts, network-runtime.test.ts (asserts the projected `process.env.NO_PROXY` value at :124), proxy-env.test.ts and network-trust-scope.test.ts (both assert `getProxyEnvVars()` output — the recommended canonicalization WILL move those expectations), apps/electron/src/main/__tests__/session-partitions-proxy.isolated.ts. NO persistence or wire boundary is crossed: the stored string `NetworkProxySettings.noProxy` (config/types.ts:31, written through storage.ts:2571) is unchanged in shape and needs no migration, and no IPC/RPC payload changes. It IS an egress-routing change, which is the repo's stated risk class: accepting a new separator makes hosts that previously traversed the corporate proxy go DIRECT — intended here, but it must be exercised on the packaged build, since resolveInterceptorBundlePath preloads the .ts source in dev and dist/interceptor.cjs when packaged.
userImpact: Concrete and silent. An operator who copies the space-separated spelling straight off the Claude Code page — `export NO_PROXY="localhost 192.168.1.1 example.com .example.com"` in the shell that launches the app, which pi-agent.ts:1466 spreads into the Pi subprocess whenever the in-app proxy is not enabled with its own noProxy (proxy-env.ts:70-73 only overwrites then) — gets ZERO bypass. Every request, including loopback RPC and local MCP servers, is forced through the corporate proxy, and the interceptor sets that proxy explicitly as Bun's `proxy:` fetch option, so it is an active reroute, not a fallback. Typing the same spelling into Settings > Network > Bypass Rules produces the same result across the Electron browser pane, the update feed and the default session partition. The only feedback is booleans: the log says `hasNoProxy: true` and the field looks accepted. Symptom the user actually sees: local/internal hosts hang or fail TLS against the corporate proxy while the bypass list plainly names them. Most users never hit it because the UI placeholder shows commas and the comma spelling works correctly.

Two things I did NOT verify from source and that rest on knowledge, both non-load-bearing for the fix: (a) Chromium's ProxyBypassRules parser separator set (I assume comma/semicolon, whitespace not a separator) — this only affects whether passing the raw string straight to Electron would have worked anyway, and the recommended fix pre-splits regardless; (b) the third-party comma-only assumption behind the RECOMMENDED proxy-env.ts canonicalization (Node/undici, Go, Python NO_PROXY parsers) — if that item is taken, sanity-check one consumer rather than trusting the claim. Also unverified: whether the interceptor bundle can import from ../config without growing the preload bundle materially; the proposed inline one-liner sidesteps the question.
